accept.reason: the update worker has a SECOND, deliberate caller: .github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml drives it directly to qualify a release ref, and CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF is that harness's own parameter, set there and read nowhere else. The rule's concern is a parameter channel that has silently stopped being delivered; this one is delivered by the workflow beside it, in the same repo, and its absence under code-work is the normal case the worker already handles (rehearsalRef null = a real cycle)

the task-code-work DESIGN is the dated record of migration #405 — it names the slot scheduler's entry point as the staging it was changing, and #974 has since deleted that module. The reference is dangling because the record is true of the moment it describes; repointing it at the queue's executor would make the document describe a design that never happened. Same standing as the per-project-scheduling entry below

the file holds the LEGACY WIRE LITERALS, which are data rather than pointers: a work item minted before the task surface moved (#1317) still carries `engine/scheduler/` in its machine block, and `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` accepts that root permanently because it is a validator — dropping it rejects that half of the ad-hoc request lane outright. The path must not resolve to a file; a decoder must keep understanding it. Collected here so this waiver is one entry rather than five across the tests that exercise the decode

the per-project-scheduling DESIGN/MIGRATION pair is the historical record of migration #394 — it names the central routine and planner files this migration deleted precisely because deleting them is what it records; rewriting those names would falsify the record, so its inbound-reference dangling is deliberate and permanent

the live canary gate names packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update because the worker is ITSELF vendored content, so a release that changes the worker cannot be rehearsed by the canary's vendored copy — that copy predates the release by definition, and a rehearsal driving it would ignore CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF entirely and run a real cycle against main, opening a PR on the canary instead of qualifying the ref. The crossing buys the one property the gate exists for: the code under test is the code every member runs the moment the release reaches them. The workflow names no pack CONTENT — only the entry point of the task that performs the converge
